answer: A refundable stake bonded to each identity resists Sybil attacks: an agent must lock funds before transacting, and the stake is slashed if the identity is caught duplicating work or voting twice. One fake identity is cheap, but an ocean of sock puppets needs a stake for each, so the attacker's cost rises linearly while honest agents pay only a temporary lock. Like a ripple from one stone, one detected fraud triggers audits of linked identities, and a zephyr of free accounts becomes a storm the attacker must fund. Reputation earned slowly and lost instantly makes the bond the real gatekeeper.
